\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کارآگاه} (kârâgâh)}{کارآگاه (kârâgâh)}]{\fa{کارآگاه} (kârâgâh) — a detective}

\label{lesson:FA-C320-karagah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be arrested, then the Persian for to detain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کارآگاه}}
\textbf{\fa{کارآگاه}} (\emph{kârâgâh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a detective\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کارآگاه} \fa{همه} \fa{چیز} \fa{را} \fa{با} \fa{دقت} \fa{نگاه} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kârâgâh hame chiz râ bâ deqqat negâh kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The detective looked at everything carefully.
\end{quote}

\emph{kâr} \textquotedblleft{}work\textquotedblright{} + \emph{âgâh} \textquotedblleft{}aware\textquotedblright{}: one who is aware of the case.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kârâgâh} is a modern compound built from Persian \emph{kâr} \textquotedblleft{}work\textquotedblright{} and \emph{âgâh} \textquotedblleft{}aware, informed\textquotedblright{}, both native words.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kârâgâh}, once more

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرنخ} (sarnakh)}{سرنخ (sarnakh)}]{\fa{سرنخ} (sarnakh) — a clue, a lead}

\label{lesson:FA-C320-sarnakh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to detain, then the Persian for a detective.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرنخ}}
\textbf{\fa{سرنخ}} (\emph{sarnakh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a clue, a lead\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پلیس} \fa{هنوز} \fa{هیچ} \fa{سرنخی} \fa{ندارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Polis hanuz hich sarnakhi nadârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police still have no clue.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}the end of the thread\textquotedblright{}: \emph{sar} \textquotedblleft{}head, end\textquotedblright{} + \emph{nakh} \textquotedblleft{}thread\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sarnakh} joins \emph{sar} \textquotedblleft{}head, end\textquotedblright{} and \emph{nakh} \textquotedblleft{}thread\textquotedblright{}, both native Persian: the loose end that leads to the rest. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to detain, then the Persian for a detective, then say \emph{sarnakh} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ردپا} (radd-e pâ)}{ردپا (radd-e pâ)}]{\fa{ردپا} (radd-e pâ) — a footprint, a trace}

\label{lesson:FA-C320-raddepa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a detective, then the Persian for a clue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ردپا}}
\textbf{\fa{ردپا}} (\emph{radd-e pâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a footprint, a trace\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{روی} \fa{برف} \fa{ردپای} \fa{یک} \fa{گرگ} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ru-ye barf radd-e pâ-ye yek gorg bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There were a wolf's footprints in the snow.
\end{quote}

\emph{radd} \textquotedblleft{}trace\textquotedblright{} + \emph{pâ} \textquotedblleft{}foot\textquotedblright{}. Also figurative: the trace someone left behind.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pâ} \textquotedblleft{}foot\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian. The origin of \emph{radd} \textquotedblleft{}trace, track\textquotedblright{} is not settled, and EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اثر} \fa{انگشت} (asar-e angosht)}{اثر انگشت (asar-e angosht)}]{\fa{اثر} \fa{انگشت} (asar-e angosht) — a fingerprint}

\label{lesson:FA-C320-asar-e-angosht}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a clue, then the Persian for a footprint.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اثر} \fa{انگشت}}
\textbf{\fa{اثر} \fa{انگشت}} (\emph{asar-e angosht}) — \textquotedblleft{}a fingerprint\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{روی} \fa{لیوان} \fa{اثر} \fa{انگشت} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ru-ye livân asar-e angosht bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There were fingerprints on the glass.
\end{quote}

\emph{asar} \textquotedblleft{}trace, mark\textquotedblright{} + \emph{angosht} \textquotedblleft{}finger\textquotedblright{}. The Arabic \emph{asar} is written with \fa{ث}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{asar} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{athar}, \textquotedblleft{}track, trace\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); \emph{angosht} \textquotedblleft{}finger\textquotedblright{} is native Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بازجویی} (bâzjuyi)}{بازجویی (bâzjuyi)}]{\fa{بازجویی} (bâzjuyi) — an interrogation, questioning}

\label{lesson:FA-C320-bazjuyi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a footprint, then the Persian for a fingerprint.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بازجویی}}
\textbf{\fa{بازجویی}} (\emph{bâzjuyi}) — \textquotedblleft{}an interrogation, questioning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بازجویی} \fa{مظنون} \fa{سه} \fa{ساعت} \fa{طول} \fa{کشید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bâzjuyi-ye maznun se sâ'at tul keshid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The questioning of the suspect took three hours.
\end{quote}

\emph{bâz} \textquotedblleft{}again\textquotedblright{} + \emph{ju} \textquotedblleft{}seeking\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{jostan} \textquotedblleft{}to seek\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Bâzjuyi kardan} is \textquotedblleft{}to interrogate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâzjuyi} joins \emph{bâz} \textquotedblleft{}again\textquotedblright{} and \emph{ju-}, the present stem of \emph{jostan} \textquotedblleft{}to seek\textquotedblright{}, with the noun suffix \emph{-i}. All of it is native Persian; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
